function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide you can copy/paste into your notebook or script to discover **and pull** ready‑to‑use object‑detection models directly from PyTorch Hub (`torch.hub`). I’ll cover both *official* torchvision models and community repositories such as Ultralytics’ YOLO series, Detectron2, MMDetection, etc., so you can pick whatever fits your latency / accuracy needs. --- ## 1️⃣ Quick “list” of what’s publicly exposed ```python import torch # List official torchvision detectors (requires internet access once per run) models = torch.hub.list("pytorch/vision", force_reload=False) print([m for m in models if "resnet" in m.lower()][:20]) # e.g. ['fasterrcnn_resnet101_fpn'] ``` > ⚠️ `torch.hub.list()` only shows top‑level modules – many repos expose sub‑modules under `/src` or `/model`. > To see everything inside a repo, clone it locally or inspect the README on GitHub. For community repos you usually know the exact tag/model name beforehand (see below). --- ## 2️⃣ Popular Object Detection Models & How to Load Them | Repo | Model | Typical Speed / Accuracy | Code | |------|-------|--------------------------|------| | `pytorch/vision` | `fasterrcnn_resnet50_fpn`, `retinanet_resnet50_fpn` | Medium speed, good COCO AP (~37–40%) | ```python
model = torch.hub.load('pytorch/vision:v0.15.1', 'fasterrcnn_resnet50_fpn', pretrained=True)
model.eval()
``` | | `pytorch/vision` | `maskrcnn_resnet50_fpn` | Slightly slower due to masks | Same pattern as above | | `ultralytics/yolov5` | `yolov5n/s/m/l/x` | Very fast (<30 ms on GPU), lower AP (~33% at yolov5l) | ```python
model = torch.hub.load('ultralytics/yolov5', 'yolov5s')
# optional: set device
device='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
model.to(device)
``` | | `ultralytics/yolo` (YOLOv8) | `yolov8n/s/m/best.pt` | Fastest, best AP ~45% on COCO | ```python
from pathlib import Path\nrepo_path=Path.home()/\"repos/ultralytics\"\n# Clone first if needed:\n# !git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics.git $repo_path\nmodel=torch.hub.load(str(repo_path),'custom','best.pt',force_reload=True)\n``` | | `facebookresearch/detectron2` | `R_50_FPN_3x` | High accuracy (~42% AP), moderate speed | Requires installing detectron2 separately:
`pip install -U git+https://github.com/facebookresearch/detectron2.git@main` then:
`from detectron2.engine import DefaultPredictor` | | `open-mmlab/mmcv-full` + `mmsegmentation` | `cascade_rcnn_r50_fpn_gconv_cascade_mask_rcnn` | State‑of‑the‑art, heavy | Install mmdeploy/MMCV first | ### TL;DR – Pick one line If you just want something that works out‑of‑the‑box: ```python # YOLOv5 small (fast, decent accuracy) model = torch.hub.load('ultralytics/yolov5', 'yolov5s', pretrained=True) model.eval() ``` Or for higher precision: ```python # Faster R‑CNN ResNet‑50 FPN (moderate speed, high accuracy) model = torch.hub.load('pytorch/vision:v0.15.1', 'fasterrcnn_resnet50_fpn', weights="DEFAULT") # uses latest pretrain model.eval() ``` --- ## 3️⃣ Running Inference All loaded models follow the same interface: call them with a batch of tensors `[B x C x H x W]`. ```python import torch from PIL import Image import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import cv2 def preprocess(img): img_tensor = torch.from_numpy(np.array(img)).permute(2,0,1).float() / 255.0 return img_tensor.unsqueeze(0) # add batch dim img = Image.open('/path/to/image.jpg').convert('RGB') inp = preprocess(img) with torch.no_grad(): outputs = model(inp)[0] boxes = outputs['boxes'].cpu().numpy() # [N,4] scores = outputs['scores'].cpu().numpy() # [N] labels = outputs.get('labels', None) # may exist for classification head # Visualise for box,scr,lbl in zip(boxes[:10], scores[:10], labels[:10]): xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax = map(int, box) cv2.rectangle(cv_img,(xmin,ymin),(xmax,ymax),(0,255,0),2) cv2.putText(cv_img,f'{scr:.2f}',(xmin,ymin-5), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX,.5,(0,255,0)) plt.imshow(cv_img); plt.axis('off'); plt.show() ``` > 👉 **Tip:** Most TorchHub models expect images normalized to `[0,1]`; if you’re feeding raw bytes, convert with `.astype(float)/255.` --- ## 4️⃣ Customizing / Fine‑Tuning Once you’ve got a base model, fine‑tune on your own dataset: ```bash # Using torchvision FasterRCNN python train.py \ --dataset coco2017_train.json \ --output-dir ./finetuned/fasterrcnn \ --epochs 12 \ --lr 0.00025 ``` See each repository’s README for training scripts—most come bundled with CLI utilities. --- ## 5️⃣ Common Pitfalls & Gotchas | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **“ModuleNotFoundError: No module named ‘detectron2’ ”** | Install detectron2 separately (`pip install -U git+...`) | | **Large download times (>100 MB)** | Use `weights=None` to skip downloading pretrained weights when you plan to re‑initialize yourself. | | **GPU memory OOM** | Reduce image resolution or batch size; switch to lighter variants (`yolov5n`, `fasterrcnn_mobilenet_v3_large_fpn`). | | **Model returns empty detections** | Ensure input tensor shape matches expectations ([C,H,W]); check normalization range. | --- ## 🎯 Bottom Line Pick a repo → grab the right model name → load with `torch.hub.load(...)` → feed a tensor → visualize results. Feel free to tell me more about your constraints (e.g., target FPS, hardware limits, required classes) and I can narrow down the perfect candidate!
